title: Benchmarking
concept: Benchmarking measures the performance impact of contracts — so you can make informed decisions about stripping vs keeping them.
why: Premature optimization is evil, but uninformed optimization is worse. Benchmark BEFORE you strip contracts to know the actual cost.
syntax_ref:
# Run benchmarks:
xiom bench

# Compare modes:
xiom bench --compare debug release

# Output shows time in ns with confidence intervals
tips: Benchmark BEFORE optimizing — measure, don't guess
Simple contracts (b != 0) cost 1-2 CPU instructions — nearly free
Contract overhead is amortized over the function's work — expensive functions see <0.1% overhead
Run benchmarks multiple times and take the average — single runs are noisy
common_mistakes: Stripping contracts without measuring their actual cost
Benchmarking contracts in debug mode (unoptimized) — measure in release with --runtime-contracts
Measuring contract overhead on a function that does almost nothing — not representative of real code
